title: Introduction to Python
description: A chapter-by-chapter course quiz. Finish each chapter to unlock the next one.

sections.title: Chapter 1 · Getting started
sections.description: What Python is, how to run it and how to write your first program.

questions.text: Who created the Python programming language?
questions.feedback: Guido van Rossum started Python in the late 1980s and released it in 1991.

questions.text: Which function displays text on the screen?
questions.feedback: print() sends output to the console in Python.

questions.text: How is Python usually described?
questions.feedback: Python is high-level and its code is run by an interpreter.

questions.text: Which symbol starts a single-line comment in Python?
questions.feedback: Everything after # on a line is ignored by Python.

sections.title: Chapter 2 · Variables and data types
sections.description: Storing values and working with numbers, text and booleans.

questions.text: Which of these is a valid variable name?
questions.feedback: Names can't start with a digit, contain hyphens or be reserved keywords such as class.

questions.text: What does type(3.14) return?
questions.feedback: Numbers with a decimal point are floats.

questions.text: What is the result of "Py" + "thon"?
questions.feedback: The + operator joins (concatenates) strings.

questions.text: Which of these is a Boolean value in Python?
questions.feedback: Python's Boolean values are True and False, with a capital first letter.

sections.title: Chapter 3 · Control flow
sections.description: Making decisions and repeating actions with if statements and loops.

questions.text: Which keyword means "else if" in Python?
questions.feedback: elif chains extra conditions after an if.

questions.text: How many times does `for i in range(3):` run its body?
questions.feedback: range(3) produces 0, 1 and 2, so the body runs three times.

questions.text: Which keyword leaves a loop immediately?
questions.feedback: break ends the loop; continue only skips to the next iteration.

questions.text: What does Python use to mark a block of code?
questions.feedback: Consistent indentation defines blocks in Python.

sections.title: Chapter 4 · Functions
sections.description: Writing reusable blocks of code with parameters and return values.

questions.text: Which keyword defines a function?
questions.feedback: Functions start with def followed by a name and parentheses.

questions.text: What does the return statement do?
options: Ends the function and sends a value back
questions.feedback: return stops the function and hands a result to the caller.

questions.text:
What does this print?

def add(a, b=2):
    return a + b

print(add(3))
questions.feedback: b defaults to 2, so add(3) returns 3 + 2 = 5.

questions.text: A variable created inside a function is called…
questions.feedback: Local variables only exist while the function runs.

questions.text: Which index returns the first item of a list?
questions.feedback: Python lists are zero-indexed.

questions.text: Which method adds an item to the end of a list?
questions.feedback: my_list.append(x) adds x at the end.

questions.text: What does a dictionary store?
questions.feedback: Dictionaries map unique keys to values.

questions.text: What does len([1, 2, 3, 4]) return?
questions.feedback: len() counts the items in the list.
